name: Datura and Brugmansia (Solanaceae)
notes: Loaded like the other catalogues (data/plants/*.json). Datura: forking annual/perennial herbs of dry disturbed ground, camps and river gravel with UPRIGHT trumpet flowers and spiny thornapple capsules. Brugmansia: small trees of Andean and tropical American forest margins and stream banks with PENDULOUS trumpets; two are extinct in the wild and only persist where people planted them, so on the planet they favour the ground near camps and old settlement stamps. Both flower at dusk, hawkmoth-pollinated (B. sanguinea hummingbird), and the heavy night scent is a pheromone source like the Amorphophallus bloom (`scent`). All are tropane-alkaloid plants: `toxic` (never eaten, never browsed: cannot_be_browsed), and `ceremonial` as for Trichocereus — the ceremony system reads the tag; 'documented' species carry a full ceremony. Silhouette rule: a Datura reads as a low forking mound with upright pale trumpets; a Brugmansia as a small dome tree with long trumpets hanging straight down — the hanging trumpets are the 64 px silhouette.
_help_realm: realm gates (design §AA): andes / south_america / north_america / south_asia; 'any' for the cosmopolitan weed D. stramonium.

shrub.name: Datura stramonium

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds lie dormant in the soil for years and flush after disturbance. Epigeal: two long, strap-like cotyledons, then broad, coarsely toothed, rank-smelling leaves on a single stout stem (green, or purple in var. tatula). By midsummer it forks repeatedly into a flat-topped bush with a white or violet trumpet in each fork.
growth.source: Wikipedia Datura stramonium (erect annual 60-150 cm; seeds dormant for years, germinate after soil disturbance; flowers all summer, 6-9 cm, open at night and visited by moths; egg-shaped capsule 3-8 cm, spiny or bald, splitting into 4); Datura genus account

repro.note: Night-opening trumpet flowers, hawkmoth pollinated; heavy sweet scent after dusk is a pheromone source like the Amorphophallus bloom.

toxic.effect: delirium, dry mouth, blindness for a day; deadly in quantity — never eaten, never browsed

shrub.source: Datura stramonium — annual weed of disturbed ground, camps, field edges and riverbanks; probably Mesoamerican, now worldwide in warm-temperate zones (Kew POWO). Tropane alkaloids; the ethnobotanical literature records ceremonial and divinatory use.

shrub.name: Datura wrightii

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two narrow cotyledons, then soft, grey-green, velvety-hairy ovate leaves. The seedling forks early into a low, sprawling, mound-shaped bush that can flower in its first summer; it builds a thick tuberous root that survives winter or drought, resprouting each year into a wider mound with huge white trumpets.
growth.source: Wikipedia Datura wrightii (vigorous herbaceous perennial 0.3-1.5 m tall and wide; fragrant white trumpets to 20 cm, often purple-edged, opening morning and evening; spiny globular capsule 3-4 cm opening when ripe; blooms Apr-Oct). Tuberous rootstock, germination and lifespan from southwestern US native-plant growers.

shrub.name: Datura metel

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two long, narrow, pointed cotyledons, then broad, soft, ovate leaves with wavy or shallowly toothed edges on a single stout green or purple-black stem. Within weeks the stem forks repeatedly into a spreading, bushy herb, with a big upright trumpet flower in each fork. In frost-free climates it can carry on as a short-lived woody-based perennial.
growth.source: Wikipedia Datura metel (annual or short-lived perennial to 1.8 m; hollow green or purple-black stems; flowers 15-20 cm, white, cream, yellow or violet, single or double; warty capsules breaking irregularly; American origin, long naturalised in Asia). Germination and timings from Datura growers.

canopy.name: Brugmansia suaveolens

growth.juvenile_note: Corky seeds sprout in 2-6 weeks with two narrow cotyledons; the seedling grows as a single straight stem with large, soft, often coarsely toothed leaves until it forks at 0.8-1.5 m; above the fork leaves are smaller, mostly entire and often lopsided at the base, and flowers appear. Fast-growing, it branches into a spreading, soft-stemmed shrub or small tree along streams and forest edges.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Brugmansia: seedlings grow on one stem to a first fork at 80-150 cm and flower only above it; plants 3-11 m; all species Extinct in the Wild, fruits now shrivel on the plant, former dispersers extinct megafauna; all parts toxic); lowland SE Brazil Atlantic Forest species; germination and growth times from growers; lifespan estimated.

repro.note: Night-opening trumpet flowers, hawkmoth pollinated; heavy sweet scent after dusk is a pheromone source like the Amorphophallus bloom.

toxic.effect: delirium, dry mouth, blindness for a day; deadly in quantity — never eaten, never browsed

canopy.name: Brugmansia sanguinea

Leaves are soft and downy; it becomes a bushy, upright small tree.
